evidence.claim: The flagged transaction (3553342, $30.91, in-person, region 494.0) carries a calibrated fraud score of cms_p=0.0249 versus the real-time risk_score of 0.55 that triggered review.

Region 494.0 is known to this card: 22 prior purchases over 18 distinct days since 2016-07-05, with the card active across 42 regions total, so the roaming-card exception applies and no home-region absence in the prior 48h (0 home, 13 other) counts as a novelty signal.
The $30.91 amount sits well inside the card's baseline (prior median $49.08, prior maximum $2,681.01 across 910+ transactions), unlike a spree above historical maximums.

The card has one prior closed case, CC-0003, a risk-score alert of the same in-person shape that was cleared as confirmed travel on 2016-07-02, indicating this cardholder's cross-region spending pattern has already been validated once.

The card also has one prior confirmed-fraud case, CC-2370 (card_not_present_fraud, opened 2016-08-20), but that episode was online and unrelated in channel and timing to this in-person, known-region purchase.

card_testing_check, under_threshold_burst and shared_origin_scan returned no card-testing chain, no just-under-$500 burst, and no shared-origin fraud signal on this card as of the flag time; the card's single historical transaction on the strong ring profile (3081282, 2016-07-22) predates this episode and the flagged transaction itself has no device record (in-person, product W).

case.summary: Verdict: legitimate at probability 0.05. Pattern is none (no fraud pattern applies) — the flagged in-person purchase (transaction 3553342, $30.91, billing region 494.0) is the sole episode item, with exposure of $0.00. The decisive evidence spans three families: history (region 494.0 is known to this card with 22 prior visits over 18 days across a 42-region roaming profile, and the amount sits comfortably inside the card's $49 median baseline), memory (the calibrated case-memory score of 0.025 sharply contradicts the triggering risk_score of 0.55, and a prior closed case, CC-0003, cleared an identically-shaped alert on this card as confirmed travel), and customer (the assumed customer_validation reply confirmed recognition of the purchase and travel to that region). We asked a customer_validation question per R1 (single weak signal, risk_score alone, probability below 0.70) and assumed a "confirm" response, as simulated evidence requests require no separate approval. An alternative reading is possible: the card does carry one prior confirmed card-not-present fraud case (CC-2370, online, August 2016), so a stricter reviewer might have pushed for step-up verification rather than an outright allow, but that prior fraud was a different channel and unrelated to this in-person, known-region activity. The bank should proceed on the auto route: CREATE_CASE to log the review, ALLOW_TRANSACTION, and CLOSE_NO_FRAUD (R3) — no escalation or block needed.
